# Starting a new repository

Every repository that uses the toolkit needs the same floor before its first line of analysis: a `.gitignore` that keeps data out and provenance in, the local checks and the hook that runs them, a test suite, the project's collaboration setting, a home for the vendored helpers, and a README and contributing guide that tell a co-author what to do on their first clone. The chapters that follow explain each piece. This one starts a repository with all of them in one call, from the toolkit's own templates, so a new project begins where the rest of the handbook expects it to be.

There are two functions, because there are two kinds of repository:

| | `create_research_project()` | `create_official_stats_project()` |
|---|---|---|
| For | a paper, an analysis, a replication package | a DW sector pipeline, an SDMX or data.unicef.org publication pipeline, a survey-processing repository |
| Canonical store for results | git: small tables and figures, each with its sidecar | the deposit (Teams and Z:), then SDMX and data.unicef.org |
| Results in the repository | committed | never: embargoed until publication |
| What is committed after a release | the results themselves; tag the submitted version | a release record, `releases/<vintage>/` |
| Code lives in | `R/` (numbered scripts) | `01_dw_prep/012_codes/<sector>/` |
| Inputs | `data/` | the deposit's `011_rawdata`; local copies in `01_dw_prep/011_rawdata/<sector>/` and `inputs/` (filled by `dw_fetch_inputs()`) |
| `.gitignore` | `research-project.gitignore` | `official-stats.gitignore` |

## Which one?

Ask where the results live and who may see them before publication. If the answer is "in git, and anyone with access to the repository may read them", it is a research project. If the results are deposited and published by the office, and nobody may see a figure before its release date, it is an official-statistics repository, however small. The difference is not cosmetic: the official-statistics template ignores output folders outright, sidecars included, and its `tools/check.R` fails on anything tracked in them, because a pre-release table committed by accident stays in git history ([Continuous integration and repository hygiene](45-ci-cd.qmd)).

A paper written from official figures after their release is a research project. A research team that also runs a production pipeline keeps the two in separate repositories.

## What each function writes

Both functions take the folder of the new repository and the collaboration model, which is required and has no default, as `dw_mode` has none: how many people may produce results is a decision for the project, not something the toolkit guesses.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### R {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```r
create_research_project(
  "C:/GitHub/learning-mobility",
  collaboration  = "multi-producer",          # or "single-producer"
  members        = c("jpazvd", "kavanesian"), # optional, informational
  title          = "Schooling Mobility Is Not Learning Mobility",
  vendor          = TRUE,                     # copy helpers from a clone ...
  toolkit_source  = "C:/GitHub/cso-toolkit",
  toolkit_version = "v0.9.1",                 # ... at this tag (default: latest)
  git             = TRUE)                     # git init, develop, hook path

create_official_stats_project(
  "C:/GitHub/DW-Nutrition",
  collaboration = "single-producer",
  vendor = TRUE, toolkit_source = "C:/GitHub/cso-toolkit")
```

#### Python {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
from cso_toolkit import create_research_project, create_official_stats_project

create_research_project(
    "C:/GitHub/learning-mobility", "multi-producer",
    members=["jpazvd", "kavanesian"],
    title="Schooling Mobility Is Not Learning Mobility",
    vendor=True, toolkit_source="C:/GitHub/cso-toolkit",
    toolkit_version="v0.9.1", git=True)

create_official_stats_project(
    "C:/GitHub/DW-Nutrition", "single-producer",
    vendor=True, toolkit_source="C:/GitHub/cso-toolkit")
```

#### Stata {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```stata
* No Stata function. Create the repository once from R or Python: the
* files are the same whichever language writes them, the .gitignore
* covers Stata's files, and the checks in tools/check.R read only files.
```

:::

A research project:

```
learning-mobility/
├── .gitignore                 research-project.gitignore, unchanged
├── profile_learning-mobility.R  sourced first by every script and session
├── .githooks/pre-push         runs tools/check.R before every push
├── cso_project.yml            collaboration: multi-producer (committed)
├── README.md                  quick start for a new co-author, layout
├── CONTRIBUTING.md            ground rules, first clone, workflow, checks
├── 00_functions/              README.md; with vendor = TRUE the helpers
│                              and .toolkit_manifest.yml
├── R/README.md                numbered scripts; R/functions/ for tested code
├── data/
│   ├── README.md              the provenance policy and the inputs table
│   ├── input_manifest.csv     file, sha256, bytes, origin, sidecar
│   └── provenance/README.md   sidecars of microdata kept outside the repo
├── output/README.md           tables and figures, each with its sidecar
├── paper/README.md            the manuscript, paper/main.tex
├── references/README.md
├── docs/README.md
├── tests/
│   ├── testthat.R             the runner (reviewer mode; sources R/functions/)
│   └── testthat/
│       ├── helper-project.R   fixtures, local state, expect_envelope()
│       └── test-project.R     cso_project.yml, manifest vs sidecars, mode
├── tools/check.R              every local check
└── .github/workflows/         only with workflows = TRUE (four, opt-in)
```

An official-statistics repository follows DW-Production and the deposit's stage numbering:

```
DW-Nutrition/
├── .gitignore                       official-stats.gitignore, unchanged
├── profile_DW-Nutrition.R           sourced first: mode, deposit paths, Z:, helpers
├── .githooks/pre-push
├── cso_project.yml                  collaboration: single-producer
├── README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md       embargo, release record, first clone
├── _config_template/user_config.yml placeholder per-person configuration
├── 00_documentation/README.md       SOPs, data flows, release checklist
├── 00_functions/                    README.md (+ helpers and manifest)
├── 01_dw_prep/
│   ├── README.md                    the stages: what each holds, what reaches git
│   ├── 010_metadata/README.md       reference metadata (codelists, maps), committed
│   ├── 011_rawdata/README.md        local raw inputs: ignored, sidecars committed
│   ├── 012_codes/README.md          pipeline code, one folder per sector
│   └── (013_wrkdata/)               local work data and outputs: ignored, embargoed
├── inputs/
│   ├── README.md                    filled from the deposit, verified
│   └── input_manifest.csv
├── releases/README.md               releases/<vintage>/, after publication
├── tests/testthat.R, tests/testthat/helper-project.R, test-project.R
├── tools/check.R                    OUTPUT_DIRS, DATA_DIRS, AUDIT_PATHS set
└── .github/workflows/               only with workflows = TRUE (three)
```

The canonical raw data, API caches and promoted work data live in the deposit (Teams `060.DW-MASTER/01_dw_prep/011_rawdata` and `013_wrkdata`), which the profile's `teamsRawData` and `teamsWrkData` point to in producer mode and redirect to the sandbox in reviewer mode ([Wiring the contract](22-wiring-the-contract.qmd)). The repository keeps folders of the same names for local work, as DW-Production does, because a sector script made by `create_sector_script()` reads `01_dw_prep/011_rawdata/<sector>/` and writes `01_dw_prep/013_wrkdata/<sector>/` relative to the repository ([Scaffolding and the contract auditor](35-scaffolding-audit.qmd)). Their contents never reach git: `.gitignore` ignores `013_wrkdata/` outright, like every output folder, and keeps only the READMEs, sidecars and manifests of `011_rawdata/`; `tools/check.R` fails on anything tracked in `013_wrkdata/` (`OUTPUT_DIRS`) and on data tracked in `011_rawdata/` (`DATA_DIRS`). `013_wrkdata/` has no tracked file at all, so it appears with the first run. `01_dw_prep/012_codes/README.md` shows how to scaffold a sector's driver against the project's own profile.

The `.gitignore`, the hook, the test helper and the workflows are the toolkit's templates byte for byte, so the rules a repository starts with are the ones the toolkit tests. Three files are set for the kind of project: `tools/check.R` (an official-statistics repository gets `OUTPUT_DIRS = "output outputs results wrk 013_wrkdata"`, the embargo check, `011_rawdata` added to `DATA_DIRS`, and `AUDIT_PATHS = "01_dw_prep/012_codes"`; the contract audit is `AUDIT_MODE = "advisory"` in a research project, where it reports raw reads such as `haven::read_dta()` without failing the checks, and `"blocking"` in official statistics, where any of them fails; see [Continuous integration and repository hygiene](45-ci-cd.qmd)), `tests/testthat.R` (which folder of function files the tests source) and `cso_project.yml` (the model, today's date and the members).

The functions never replace a file silently. Before writing anything they compare every target with what they would write: a file with the same bytes is left alone and reported as `unchanged`, and a file with different content stops the whole call, with nothing written, unless `overwrite = TRUE`. Both return the list of files with their status (`written`, `overwritten`, `unchanged`), so a second identical call changes nothing and says so. To adopt the conventions in an existing repository, follow [Onboarding a repo](42-onboarding-example.qmd), or create a scaffold in an empty folder and copy what you need.

### The options

- **`vendor`, `toolkit_source`, `toolkit_version`.** `vendor` is `FALSE` by default. `TRUE` copies the helpers into `00_functions/` from a release tag of a git clone of cso-toolkit (`toolkit_source`, or `CSO_TOOLKIT_ROOT`), and writes `.toolkit_manifest.yml` with that tag as `pulled_version` and the commit it points to as `pulled_commit` ([The vendoring model](41-vendoring.qmd)). The tag is `toolkit_version`, by default the clone's latest release tag (`v0.9.1`, never a pre-release such as `v1.0.0-rc1`). The files are read from the tag's commit in the clone's history, never from its working tree, so a clone on another branch or with local edits still vendors exactly the released bytes; a tag the clone does not have stops the call before anything is written (`git fetch --tags` first). The default set is `dw_io.R`, `dw_api.R`, `cso_toolkit_sync.R`, `dw_provenance.R`, `dw_deposit.R`, `dw_project.R`, `test_scripts.R` and `zzz.R`, plus `profile_helpers.R` and `create_sector_script.R` for official statistics; a helper of that set which the tag does not have yet (`dw_project.R` before the release that adds it) is skipped and named in a message. A character vector picks the files, all of which must exist at the tag, and the three that `tools/check.R` needs are always added. Without vendoring, `tools/check.R` leaves out the `contract-audit` and `vintage` checks, with a comment saying to add them back once `00_functions/` is filled.
- **`workflows`.** `FALSE` by default: checks run locally. `TRUE` adds the GitHub Actions workflows, which call the same `tools/check.R` and by default run only when started by hand and on pull requests into `main`.
- **`git`.** `FALSE` by default. `TRUE` runs `git init` with `develop` as the first branch (`main` is created at the first release), sets `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks`, and stages the hook with its executable bit so it also runs on macOS and Linux clones. It never commits, creates a remote or pushes.

### The profile

Every repository gets `profile_<project>.R`, named after its folder, the script every analysis script and interactive session sources first, as `profile_DW-Production.R` is in DW-Production ([Scaffolding and the contract auditor](35-scaffolding-audit.qmd)). Both kinds are written from one template, `templates/profile/profile.R`, and both pass `review_profile()`:

- it reads `~/.config/user_config.yml` the way DW-Production's template lays it out, the user's block first (`user_config[[USERNAME]]`), top-level keys as a fallback;
- it resolves `dw_mode` as `dw_mode_by_project[["<project>"]]`, then `dw_mode`, with no default; when neither is set it stops and shows the lines to add, with the user name filled in;
- it sources the vendored helpers from `00_functions/`, `zzz.R` first, and reads the vintage from `.toolkit_manifest.yml`;
- it never installs a package: a missing one stops the session with the list to install;
- it resolves the collaboration model from `cso_project.yml` and ends with the sentinel `profile_<project> <- TRUE`, which sector scripts test before they run.

The official-statistics profile adds the deposit paths of [Wiring the contract](22-wiring-the-contract.qmd): `teamsRawData` and `teamsWrkData` point to Teams `060.DW-MASTER` under the user's `teamsRoot` for a producer, and to `sandboxRoot` for a reviewer, with the `*Canonical` aliases kept for reads; and it checks the Z: mirror with a probe that cannot hang on a disconnected drive, without stopping when the mirror is missing. Its `user_config.yml` keys are in `_config_template/user_config.yml`.

## First steps for the person who created it

1. Fill in the paragraphs the README leaves as comments: the question or the indicators, the authors, the outlet or the publication channel.
2. Vendor the helpers if you did not (`00_functions/README.md`), and run `Rscript --no-init-file tools/check.R`. Every line should pass.
3. Stage by path and make the first commit on `develop`; create `main` from it when you first release or circulate a version.
4. Create the remote (private unless the project says otherwise), push both branches, make `develop` the default branch and protect both trunks, so changes reach them only through pull requests (`docs/git_workflow.md`).

## First clone, for a co-author

The generated `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` carry these steps, so a co-author can follow them without this chapter:

1. Clone, then `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, once, so the checks run on every push.
2. In `~/.config/user_config.yml`, under their user name, set `dw_mode: reviewer`. They switch to `producer` only for a session in which they deliberately produce or refresh results (for this repository alone: `dw_mode_by_project:` with the repository's name). In an official-statistics repository they also set `teamsRoot` and a `sandboxRoot` outside the repository (`_config_template/user_config.yml`). `source("profile_<project>.R")` then tells them what is still missing.
3. Obtain the inputs under their own licence (research) or fill `inputs/` with `dw_fetch_inputs()` (official statistics), and verify that the bytes match the manifest: then their results are built from the same inputs.
4. Run `Rscript --no-init-file tools/check.R`.
5. In a multi-producer project, add their handle under `members:` in `cso_project.yml` in their first pull request.

## The collaboration setting

`cso_project.yml` records how many people may produce results. In a `single-producer` project one person produces and the others review; in a `multi-producer` project every co-author may produce, always through a pull request, and `dw_save()` refuses to replace an output that was changed outside it or written by someone else during the session, unless the producer passes `takeover = TRUE` after checking. The setting is committed, so it is the same for everyone; a person's `dw_mode` stays in their own configuration. Change it later with `dw_set_collaboration()`, in one reviewed pull request ([Roles and the mode contract](21-roles-and-modes.qmd), "Collaboration model").

## Local checks first

The repository starts with checks that run on the author's machine: `tools/check.R` runs every check with one command and the pre-push hook runs it before each push. GitHub Actions are opt-in (`workflows = TRUE`) and run the same script; by default they run only when started by hand and on release pull requests into `main`, so routine work costs no Actions minutes. The pull request carries the output of `tools/check.R` for its head commit, and that record is the gate.
